items: Lighting/traffic/water assets vendor-siloed; data not shared.
Faults reported by citizens; maintenance unscheduled.
Public-space sensing raised privacy concerns; governance missing.

blocks.x: The urban telemetry fabric brought multi-vendor assets into governed streams with privacy-by-design tags; condition-based maintenance orchestration schedules work citywide; and the urban OT security program (segmentation, monitoring) protected public systems — governance evidence accepted by the data-protection authority.

Delivery followed the standard rhythm — Diagnose with a signed baseline, Prove with falsifiable criteria, Industrialize with staged rollouts — while the control evidence (model cards, decision replay, security tests) accumulated as artifacts of the build.
